rgb: The scene is an elevated outdoor construction edge bordered by a grey concrete wall on the left, wooden scaffolding poles in front, and another brick building within arm's reach, roughly 0.5 to 1.5 metres away across the ground below. On the ledge far out of arm's reach (3 to 5 metres) in front of the camera wearer are stacked red bricks and a small blue bucket, while metal mortar pans and bricks rest on the scaffolding to the lower man's right within 1 to 3 metres of him. In the fourth and fifth frames, the man below reaches his gloved left arm upward away from the camera wearer's right hand, which enters the lower-right distance holding a brick 3 to 5 metres from the camera and out of the outstretched reach of the man below. The lower body of the man on the scaffolding is partially occluded by the ledge and wooden poles throughout the sequence, and the camera wearer's body remains out of view except for their right hand and a glimpse of their foot in the final frame.
depth: The monocular depth map depicts an elevated construction ledge where a vertical wall on the left (3 to 5 m away) and horizontal floor slab on the lower right (3 to 5 m away) sit far outside the immediate foreground, separated by wooden scaffolding poles (3 to 5 m away) from a worker standing below on lower scaffolding and a background building and street within arm's reach, under 1.5 m away. Across the five frames, the camera wearer leans backward and tilts downward over the ledge as the worker below moves away upward from roughly 0.5–1.5 m away in frame 1 to about 3–5 m in frames 4 and 5, while extending his left arm to 3–5 m away and out of reach of the camera. In frame 5, the camera wearer's own right hand holding a brick enters the bottom-right distance at roughly 3–5 m, far outside arm's reach of both the wearer and the worker's outstretched glove about 3–5 m behind it, while the worker's lower body remains occluded beneath the ledge and scaffolding throughout. The depth map clearly separates the crisscrossing distant scaffolding poles and the worker's extended arm from the visually cluttered brick building and ground close behind them, which blend together in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable on nearby background structures under 1.5 m away—collapsing the opposite building, trees, and street into uniform black—and blurs depth boundaries slightly around thin ropes and between the brick and the worker's separated hand in frame 5.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the worker below the camera wearer as a single 'person' mask positioned slightly right of center in frame 1 (about 0.5–1.5 m away, within reach, and below the ledge) and shifting toward the upper-center/left in frames 4 and 5 as the camera tilts down and the worker moves farther away to 3–5 m. The worker's silhouette shows his torso facing downward away from the camera wearer while his lower body is occluded by the concrete ledge in frames 1–2 and by wooden scaffolding poles in frames 3–5. Across frames 3 to 5, the mask captures his left arm extending upward and to the right away from the camera wearer, moving out of arm's reach (3–5 m away) in frame 4 and separating from the camera wearer's right hand and brick (about 3–5 m away) in the bottom-right corner of frame 5. This map makes it easy to track the contiguous contour of the worker's upper body and outstretched arm against the busy bamboo scaffolding and sunlit foreground without visual distraction. However, it is highly unreliable for scene layout and objects: it completely misses the scaffolding, walls, metal pans, bricks in frames 1–2, a second partially visible person on the near left of frame 3 (roughly 0.5–1.5 m away and within reach), and the camera wearer's hand in frame 5, while misclassifying the held brick and hand in frame 5 as a 'hot dog' and briefly hallucinating a tiny secondary mask far from the worker in frame 2.
pose: The pose map renders 2D yellow body keypoints and limb segments for the worker standing below the camera wearer, tracking his position from the lower-right at 0.5–1.5 m distance and within reach in frame 1 to the center and upper-left at 3–5 m distance and out of reach in frames 3 through 5. The arrangement of the head, eye/ear, and shoulder keypoints shows the worker facing and looking downward away from the camera wearer across the sequence, with his torso angled beneath the ledge while his legs remain unmapped or occluded below the scaffolding. While his arms are bent far from his torso (about 2.5–3.0 m away) in frames 1 and 2, the left shoulder, elbow, and wrist keypoints extend sharply downward-right in the image plane from frame 3 onward, bringing his left magenta hand skeleton in frame 4 to 3–5 m away and out of the camera wearer's arm's reach. The skeleton explicitly reveals the joint articulations of the worker's shoulders, elbows, and torso orientation even where dark shadows and overlapping scaffolding poles obscure his body in the RGB frames. Conversely, the pose map is unreliable in capturing full-body and multi-person geometry: it hallucinates cramped leg keypoints on the occluded lower body in frames 1 and 2, misses the worker's right forearm holding a pan in frames 4 and 5, drops the magenta hand skeleton in frame 5, and fails to detect both the camera wearer's reaching right hand in frame 5 (at 3–5 m) and the partially visible person on the left edge of frame 3.
